tagline: Up the Nestucca through the rain forest, with the log trucks.
intro: From Beaver on the coast highway, Blaine Road turns inland and in seven miles reaches the byway, which follows the Nestucca River up through a wooded canyon in the Coast Range toward Carlton. The canyon walls are old seafloor sandstone and basalt, weathered and covered with lichen, worts and moss. About 120 inches of rain a year keep the woods a temperate rain forest.
It is a slow road, open all year, though snow and ice can make it hazardous. Log trucks use it in every season, and there is no cell signal in the drainage.

moments.title: Beaver
moments.text: A post office since 1889 on US 101 and the Nestucca, named, like a good many places in the Oregon Country, for the animal the pioneers admired for its industry.

moments.title: Alder Glen
moments.text: One of four riverside campgrounds along the road, where Alder Glen Falls can be watched from a campsite on the Nestucca.

moments.title: Carlton
moments.text: Wilson Carl kept the first post office and stagecoach stop seven miles west, but the railroad stayed this side of the mountain and the town grew up around the tracks.

sources.label: FHWA America's Byways, Nestucca River Back Country Byway
